bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices guide. No manufacturer manual exists for this model, so we built this from general best practices for this type of firearm. It does not represent manufacturer data. If you obtain the factory manual, follow it over this guide. Never take a firearm further apart than this guide goes unless its maker documents it.
cleanIntro:
No manual from Falkor Defense exists for this model, so this guide works from the pattern the Falkor Defense Petra is built on — the AR — which field strips the same way on every rifle of the kind. It clears the rifle, asks you to confirm by sight that yours is built that way, then takes it down as far as the bolt. If what you see does not match, the strip stops and the rifle is cleaned with the action locked open.

Listed in Fieldstrip as .308. The chambering marked on the gun itself is the one that counts — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the room, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before you start, put every loose cartridge, loaded magazine and box of ammunition in another room — a cleaning bench with live rounds on it is where unintended discharges happen. Keep the muzzle pointed where a shot would hurt no one, and keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time. Wear eye protection whenever you use solvent or work near a spring, and work where the air moves.
steps.prose: A safety, if yours has one, is never a substitute for an empty chamber, and nothing in this guide relies on one.

steps.title: Magazine out, bolt back and locked
steps.action: Press the magazine release and take the magazine out first. Pull the charging handle fully back, press the bottom of the bolt catch on the left of the receiver to lock the bolt open, and push the charging handle back home. If the bolt will not lock back, hold it back by the handle. Keep your hand and thumb out of the bolt's path.
steps.prose: A selector, if your rifle has one, goes to safe if it will — but it is never a substitute for an empty chamber.

steps.title: Look, then feel — and do it twice
steps.action: With the action open, look into the chamber and up into the empty magazine well, then put a fingertip into the chamber: a cartridge that hides in a dark chamber cannot hide from a finger. Close the action under control, open it again, and check the same way a second time.
steps.prose: ⛔ If anything will not come out, stop: never pry it out with a tool, and contact Falkor Defense with the gun pointed somewhere safe.

steps.title: Confirm it is built the AR way
steps.action: With the rifle empty and the bolt locked back, look for three things: two pins running across the lower receiver — one at the front, just ahead of the magazine well, and one at the rear, above the pistol grip; a T-shaped charging handle at the back of the upper receiver; and the upper and lower receivers meeting along a seam you can see. If all three are there, carry on.
steps.prose: ⛔ If any of them is missing, or you are not sure, this is where your strip ends: go straight to the cleaning steps and clean the bore from the muzzle with the action locked open.

steps.title: Rear pin across, upper hinged open
steps.action: Press the top of the bolt catch and let the bolt go forward. Push the rear takedown pin from the left side to the right until it stops — it is held captive and does not come all the way out, so never force it further. Then swing the upper receiver forward and up on the front pin, like a hinge.
steps.prose: If the rear pin will not move with firm thumb pressure, a nylon or brass punch is the right tool — never a steel one on the receiver.

steps.title: Bolt carrier group and charging handle out the back
steps.action: With the upper hinged open, draw the charging handle back a few centimetres; the bolt carrier group comes back with it and can be drawn straight out of the rear of the upper. Then draw the charging handle further back and drop it down out of its track. Lay both on a clean cloth.

steps.title: The bolt out of the carrier
steps.action: Push the bolt fully back into the carrier. Pull the firing pin retaining pin out of the left side of the carrier, tip the carrier back, and let the firing pin slide out of the rear. Turn the cam pin a quarter turn and lift it out of the top, then draw the bolt out of the front of the carrier.
steps.prose: Note which way the bolt faced before you take it out — it goes back the same way. Keep the three small parts together: a carrier group missing its cam pin, its firing pin or its retaining pin must never go back into the rifle.

steps.title: That is the whole strip
steps.action: Nothing else comes apart. The extractor and its pin, the gas rings, the gas key and its screws, the buffer and spring in the stock, the trigger group and the barrel stay exactly as they are — those are work for Falkor Defense. The front pin stays in, holding the two receivers together.

steps.title: The bore, from the chamber end
steps.action: With the upper hinged open and the carrier out, the bore is open from the rear. Push a brush wet with bore solvent from the chamber end through to the muzzle, a few passes, then dry patches until they come out clean. A rod guide in the rear of the upper keeps the rod centred. Finish with a lightly oiled patch for storage, and run a dry patch through before you shoot.
steps.prose: The crown — the edge of the muzzle — is what decides where the shot goes; a rod dragged across it does lasting harm.

steps.title: The chamber and the locking lugs
steps.action: Use a chamber brush, or a patch on a small brush, to clean the chamber and the ring of locking lugs just behind it, where carbon collects. Wipe out the inside of the upper receiver, then wipe the inside of the lower dry around the hammer — solvent stays out of the trigger group.

steps.title: Bolt, carrier and firing pin
steps.action: Scrape the carbon off the tail of the bolt and out of the inside of the carrier with a nylon brush and a little solvent, and wipe the bolt face. Wipe the firing pin clean and dry — it goes back with no oil on it. Then put a light film of oil on the outside of the bolt body, the cam pin, and the outside of the carrier where it rides in the receiver.
steps.prose: A dry, carboned bolt is the most common reason a rifle of this pattern stops running; an oily firing pin collects grit where it matters most.

steps.title: Look for the things that mean stop
steps.action: Hold the barrel up to the light and look through it: you want a clean, unbroken bore with no obstruction, no bulge and no dark ring. Look over the bolt's lugs, the receivers and the stock for cracks, chips on the lugs, wear at the cam pin hole, and for anything loose or missing. A screw or pin that has worked loose is reported, not tightened — how tight it should be is a question for Falkor Defense.
steps.prose: Any one of these means the gun is not fired until Falkor Defense has seen it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Falkor Defense Petra, and this guide will not invent one. No manual from Falkor Defense exists for this model, so nothing about the inside of it can be known from a document. Anything that needs more than this guide goes to Falkor Defense, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Brush wet with bore solvent from the chamber end, then dry patches until clean
Chamber and locking lugs with a chamber brush
A lightly oiled patch for storage; a dry patch before the next shot

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Carbon off the bolt tail and out of the carrier
Firing pin wiped clean and DRY
A light film of oil on the bolt body, the cam pin and the carrier's outside

cleaning.name: RECEIVERS
tasks: Inside of the lower wiped dry
⛔ No solvent into the trigger group

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped with a lightly oiled cloth
No solvent on wood, finishes or optics

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored dry — never shut in a closed case while damp
Looked over for rust at every clean

reassembly: The bolt into the front of the carrier, facing the way it came out, and pushed fully back.
The cam pin dropped into the top and turned a quarter turn back; the firing pin slid into the rear; the retaining pin pushed back in from the left.

⛔ Check the group before it goes in: tip it rear-end down — the firing pin must not fall out — and draw the bolt forward — it must stop, held by the cam pin. A group that fails either check does not go into the rifle.
The charging handle lifted into its track and pushed in part way; the carrier group slid in behind it; both pushed fully home together.
The upper swung closed on the front pin, and the rear pin pushed back from the right until it seats.
fncheck: Magazine out and the chamber empty. Pull the charging handle back and let it go: the bolt runs fully back and closes fully forward, and it locks open on an empty magazine. The selector, if your rifle has one, moves through each of its positions with the hammer back. This check never asks you to pull the trigger.
